title: Excessive Configuration Export (Over-Configuration)
damaged_code:
```rust
struct CacheConfig {
    initial_capacity: usize,
    max_capacity: usize,
    cleanup_interval_ms: u64,
    eviction_threshold_ratio: f32,
    concurrency_level: usize,
    hash_seed: u64,
    // 50+ other tuning micro-parameters
}
```
pattern: Moving internal complexity upwards by exporting dozens of private tuning micro-parameters to users under the guise of "flexibility," instead of designing stable, self-tuning internal algorithms.
why_bad: Heavy cognitive load on users. Instead of having a clean, simple interface, users must research and specify values for dozens of parameters they do not understand, resulting in fragile, poorly tuned systems. It represents a direct failure of the class to hide its implementation details.
detection: Identify configuration structs containing more than 15 fields, particularly when most of those parameters have no obvious or documented impact on standard execution.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Low-level database engines, operating systems, or game engines where extreme manual hardware tuning is a primary feature.
fix: Choose sensible, self-tuning defaults. Keep the public configuration minimal, and hide micro-tuning parameters internally.
source: *John K. Ousterhout - A Philosophy of Software Design (2018)*, Chapter 8, "Example: configuration parameters".
